articles.title: Eastgate Gets $18,500 for Bike Repair Clinic
articles.deck: Residents of Eastgate filled the hall on Monday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The Eastgate Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library. The group has raised $18,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Monday mornings. The plan calls for bike repair clinic along Prospect Terrace, with work expected to start in June.
Public works estimates the work will take about 31 weeks once it begins. Yolanda Galloway, who has lived in Eastgate for 31 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: Council Approves $18,500 for Coal Court Repairs
articles.deck: The vote came after 38 residents spoke at Friday’s session.
body: Residents of Tannery Flats said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. Public works estimates the work will take about 38 weeks once it starts in July.
Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

Councilmember Nora Thibodeaux asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $18,500. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.

articles.title: Jolene Rasmussen, 91, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Jolene Rasmussen for the many years of service to Mill Hill.
body: Born in Mill Hill in the years after the war, Jolene Rasmussen spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to St. Brendan’s Parish in his or her name.
Jolene Rasmussen died in April at home on Dover Road, at the age of 91.
